mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle, reducing discount rates on corporate bonds and boosting equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in <30% of triggered instances during tightening cycles (p > 0.05 in t-test), or FEDFUNDS does not decline for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in the federal funds rate above 2.5% triggers investor concerns about inflation, reducing risk appetite and generating negative S&P 500 forward returns within the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns remain negative for <40% of triggered instances when FEDFUNDS stays above 2.5% for >1 month, or the 5-day return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent monthly increases in consumer demand (GDPC1) and labor participation (PAYEMS) signal robust economic growth, boosting corporate earnings expectations and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > previous month AND PAYEMS > previous month
failure_condition: SPX returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) in >70% of triggered instances, or the 60-day returns are not higher than a baseline of 1.0%.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, sustained CPIAUCSL below 2% suggests controlled inflation, maintaining investor confidence in equity growth and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) in >60% of late-cycle instances, or CPIAUCSL exceeds 2% in >30% of the period.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in unemployment rate above 5% signals weakening labor market strength, prompting central banks to raise rates and reducing equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns within the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns remain negative for <50% of triggered instances when UNRATE stays above 5% for >1 month, or the 5-day return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) both increasing in the same month signal robust supply-side growth, boosting corporate profits and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > previous month AND HOUST > previous month
failure_condition: SPX returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) in >60% of triggered instances, or the 20-day returns are not higher than a baseline of 1.0%.

mechanism_narrative: In a post-recession recovery phase, rising retail sales (RSAFS) alongside elevated industrial production (INDPRO) signals improving demand, fostering optimism about corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) in >80% of post-recession instances, or the 60-day returns are not higher than a baseline of 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in labor participation (PAYEMS) below 135,000 signals weakening labor market engagement, prompting central banks to maintain tight policies and generating negative S&P 500 forward returns within the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns remain negative for <50% of triggered instances when PAYEMS stays below 135,000 for >2 months, or the 5-day return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).
